paragraphs: Friend, this is a heavy one, and I'm not going to dress it up. God says the iniquity of Israel and Judah is "exceedingly great," and He says it right after showing Ezekiel idols at His own temple (Ezekiel 9:9; 8:3-16). The people were saying, "The LORD has forsaken the land; the LORD does not see" (Ezekiel 9:9). The passage answers that one plainly: He saw all of it, and He will bring their deeds down upon their own heads (Ezekiel 9:10).

But look at the one man in linen with the writing kit. Before a single weapon moves, God sends him through the city to put a mark on the foreheads of the men "sighing and groaning over all the abominations committed there" (Ezekiel 9:4). Nobody who grieved over the sin was lost in the crowd, because God told the six, "do not go near anyone who has the mark" (Ezekiel 9:6). I think that's a gentle thing to hold onto, baker: God notices the ones who hurt over what is wrong.

So what do we take to the oven? God is holy, and He takes sin seriously, even when it's sitting in the very place meant to honor Him. He also sees every sigh and every groan, and He knows who is His. Ezekiel fell facedown and cried out, and I think that's a good way to hold a hard passage like this one (Ezekiel 9:8). And this vision isn't over yet, friend.
